root_cause:
Classification: (b), a stale hardcoded pin. It is not (a), a source regression, and not (c), a bug in the new strict/declared semantics.

The seven was never a free-standing fact. The control population comes from original_raster_host_ancestry_census (tools/diag_gptmax_raster_host_source_membership.py:673-675). That function skips every opening trace that has a host_wall_id and keeps only corroborated openings whose reason codes contain `raster_source_band_`. The cardinality is therefore "unhosted G17 openings", which is 21 claims minus hosted claims: 21-14=7 before, 21-15=6 now.

When the source-authenticated 1215 opening (physical_opening_existence_2b2a91e8...) became hosted, the count legitimately fell to six. The Lot16 declaration in tools/declared_additive_source_retention.json covers exactly this event.

The zero-endpoint workflow's path filter (lines 5-14) does not list the host producers or tools/diag_gptmax_raster_host_source_membership.py. The 1215 landing therefore never re-ran it, and the stale 14 and 7 sat until #2713 touched the file. In the pre-PR workflow the 14-host pin sat inside strict_or_declared. With baseline == candidate (snapshot 3fcb6bc5 on both sides) no declaration can match, so that pin would have failed on main as well.

claims.claim: The 144-DPI 'solid and unchanged' positive can rest on a handful of pixels, and the join silently drops some inputs.
claims.evidence: Of the 30 edges, 12 have at most 5 interior pixel samples, and 10 of those report original_144_solid_and_unchanged=True. All 10 raster_wall_band_end edges have 2-4 samples and 8 are True. No minimum sample size or typed insufficient status exists in _source_144_pixel_profile. MASS_THRESHOLD=200 (pb_raster_opening_source_primitives.py:32, tuned for 300 DPI) is reused unchanged at 144 DPI, where a half-covered pixel reads as ink. unchanged_rgb_sample_count equals pixel_sample_count for all 30, so the images-only versus full-render disagreement check is never rejected on real data. In pb_g17_dual_dpi_source_correspondence_shadow.py: (1) _axis_line returns None for non-axis-aligned W4 or G17 geometry, so those fragments are dropped without a count (only len(w4_edges) is reported); (2) source_edges[str(f.edge_id)] is last-wins on a duplicate edge id (the collision is recorded but the earlier edge is lost); (3) the lattice tolerance is 72/144+72/300 = 0.74 pt, applied per fragment with `overlap > tol`, so splitting a W4 line into fragments shorter than 0.74 pt would remove it from the join. The unit-test comment says '0.5 pt is exactly one pixel' while the constant is 0.74, and the boundary tests sit only at 0.5 and 0.75.
